annotations.title: Save, restore or re-rule a workbook

description: Saves, replaces, restores or re-rules a workbook directly, with no run. Save text you edited (`document`, or `sheets`, with the `base_version` you read); restore or undo to an earlier version (`restore_version` alone — no need to read first); or set its schema, the rules every edit must hold (`schema` alone, e.g. dates must be YYYY-MM-DD). Write in the workbook's form: read_workbook's `file_type` and `edit_as` say what its tabs hold — markdown for docx, a table per sheet for xlsx, one svg per slide for pptx, LaTeX/Typst for an editable pdf, glTF JSON for glb. Every save is compiled to that file type and against the schema; a failing one is refused with each error's tab and line. `check_only` compiles the same edit (text, tabs or schema) and says what a save would be told, saving nothing: check, fix, then save. Many writers filling one table divide it with `claim`: rows nobody else has, handed to you in one call. A 3D (glb) workbook also comes back with a picture of the model, from the angles in `views` (or `azimuth`/`elevation`), so you can see what an edit did.

agent.description: With `claim`: your name as the Claims tab shows it, one per agent (e.g. agent3).

azimuth.description: For a 3D workbook: one picture from this angle round the model, in degrees from the front (90 is the right side). Instead of `views`.

base_schema_version.description: With `schema`: the schema version you read; 0 where it had none.

base_version.description: The version you read and changed.

check_only.description: true to compile this edit and say what a save would be told, without saving.

claim.description: When several agents or people fill one table at once: take this many of its rows (1-50) that nobody has claimed and that still have an empty cell. They are written to the workbook's Claims tab under `agent` and come back as a table, with the version to write on; no one else is given them. Fill them and write the tab as usual. Answers with no rows when every row is taken. Needs `tab` and `agent`.

document.description: The new text of a one-tab workbook.

elevation.description: With `azimuth`: degrees above the horizon (0 level, 89 from above).

from_file.description: An uploaded file (/attachments/<workbook>/<name>, as create_workbook's or upload's link names it, or a drive path) made the workbook's next version through its file type's import — its first, or a revised file (a remodelled .glb, a new export of the spreadsheet) over earlier versions, which stay restorable. To revise a workbook from a new file: upload it to /attachments/<this workbook>/<name>, then this.

image_width.description: For a 3D workbook: the picture's width in pixels, 256 to 1024. Default 768.

restore_version.description: An earlier version to make current again, as a new version.

schema.description: The whole new schema: a ```tables fence of JSON, and optionally a ```tla module.

sheets.description: The tabs you change, add or remove; the others are kept. Tab ids come from read_workbook's `tabs`.

id.description: An existing tab's id. Omit to add a new tab.

markdown.description: The tab's new content. Omit to keep it as it is.

name.description: A new name for the tab, or the name of a new tab.

remove.description: True removes the tab with this id.

tab.description: With `claim`: the tab whose table is divided, by id or name.

views.description: For a 3D (glb) workbook: the angles to picture the model from, up to 4. Default one three-quarter view (its own camera when it has one).

name: write_workbook
